note — the bold part is what the card te: ich kann: modal verbs have no -e in the ich form, and the vowel changes in the singular.
du kannst: a, not ö, in the singular.
er/sie kann: no -t, the same as ich kann.
wir können: the plural keeps the ö of the infinitive.
ihr könnt: ö plus -t.
Sie können, then the infinitive at the end.
nicht goes just before the infinitive at the end.
ich muss: no -e, and ü becomes u in the singular.

English: You **have to** pay the bill. (one friend)
note — the bold part is what the card te: du musst: u, and -st.
er muss, the same as ich muss.
sie muss + the infinitive fragen at the end.
wir müssen: the plural keeps the ü.
ihr müsst: ü plus -t.
nicht müssen means don't have to, never mustn't.
ich will means I want: not the English future will.
du willst: o becomes i in the singular.
er will, no -t. wollen can take just an object, with no infinitive.
er will + spielen at the end.
wir wollen. Urlaub machen: to go on holiday.
ihr wollt: o plus -t.
sie wollen: the plural keeps the o.
The modal stands second and the infinitive goes to the very end; together they bracket the sentence.
Everything else goes inside the bracket: müssen … kaufen.

English: She wants to **visit** her grandma on Sunday.
German: Sie will am Sonntag ihre Oma **besuchen**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: The infinitive comes last, after the time and the object.

English: Today I have to **write** a letter.
note — the bold part is what the card te: heute first, the modal second, ich third, the infinitive last.
In a yes/no question the modal opens and the infinitive closes.

English: Why do you want to **stay**? (one friend)
note — the bold part is what the card te: Question word, modal, subject, then the infinitive at the end.
nicht stays before the infinitive.
kann second, warten last.

English: On Monday we have to **work** at eight.
German: Am Montag müssen wir um acht **arbeiten**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: The day first, the modal second, wir, the time, then the infinitive.

English: Do you want to **go** on holiday in July? (formal)
note — the bold part is what the card te: Urlaub machen splits: Urlaub inside the bracket, machen at the end.
nicht after the definite object, before the infinitive.
müssen second, bezahlen last.
The infinitive is never in second place: it waits for the end.
wer, the modal, then the infinitive.
The infinitive keeps its plain form: lesen, never liest.
